content.heading: PIL under Article 226
content.text: A bona fide public-interest petitioner may invoke Article 226 of the Constitution to move a High Court for enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose within the High Court's territorial jurisdiction. Liberalised standing under PIL practice applies, but the petition must still disclose a genuine public interest and a legal or constitutional wrong amenable to writ relief. Private disputes dressed as PIL are not maintainable. Article 226 is wider in subject-matter than Article 32 but remains subject to territorial limits and judicial restraint against abuse.
